eventMetadata.context_description: Thunder's decisive 123-85 Game 1 victory over the Lakers on May 5 establishes a 1-0 lead in the Western Conference semifinals, reflecting their superior depth despite Jalen Williams sidelined by a hamstring strain from the first-round sweep of the Suns. The top-seeded Thunder (64-18), defending their home-court advantage with Game 2 on May 7 at Paycom Center, dominated all four regular-season meetings by an average 39.5 points. Lakers (53-29), who ousted the Rockets 4-2 in round one, face mounting challenges without Luka Doncic (Grade 2 hamstring, week-to-week recovery) and rely heavily on LeBron James amid back-to-back road tests and injury concerns for Austin Reaves.

title: 2026 FIFA World Cup Winner

eventMetadata.context_description: In Game 1 of the Eastern Conference semifinals, top-seeded Detroit Pistons host the Cleveland Cavaliers at Little Caesars Arena, where home-court advantage and regular-season Eastern Conference lead shape trader consensus amid the Pistons' momentum from a dramatic first-round comeback over Orlando—their first playoff series win since 2008. Cleveland advanced past Toronto behind Jarrett Allen's dominant 22 points and 19 rebounds in the clincher, showcasing frontcourt strength. Pre-game injury reports were clean for Cleveland, while Pistons ruled out backup Kevin Huerter (left adductor strain), a minor depth hit. Recent head-to-head games split evenly, highlighting a competitive matchup with Cade Cunningham's playmaking pivotal for Detroit in this best-of-seven series.

title: Iran closes its airspace by...?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if Iran initiates a major closure of its airspace, that is not solely due to weather conditions, by the listed date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

A “major closure” is defined as a broad closure, cancellation, or suspension of commercial flights transiting, arriving in, and departing from Iranian airspace or a major Iranian Airspace region. A qualifying closure must apply generally to flights across Iran or a major Iranian airspace region. Limited cancellations, delays, or other partial closures will not qualify. Limited exceptions to a broad closure, however, will not disqualify such a closure from counting (e.g. exceptions for certain flights pre-approved by the Iranian Civil Aviation Authority may be permitted). 

Any non-weather complete suspension of commercial arrivals and departures affecting at least two of the following airports will qualify: Imam Khomeini International Airport (IKA), Mehrabad Airport (THR), Mashhad International Airport (MHD), Shiraz International Airport (SYZ), or Isfahan International Airport (IFN).

Qualifying previous examples include the January 2026 total closure of Iranian airspace except to international flights with express governmental permission (https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/iran-shuts-airspace-most-flights-flightradar24-says-2026-01-14/) and the April 2024 closure of Iran’s western airspace (https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/iranian-airports-cancel-flights-until-monday-morning-2024-04-14/). Non-qualifying examples include the January 27, 2026 partial closure of Iranian airspace around the Strait of Hormuz (https://www.aa.com.tr/en/middle-east/iran-issues-airspace-notice-for-military-drills-near-strait-of-hormuz/3812508) and the January 25 - April 25, 2026 VFR (Visual Flight Rules) flights suspension which did not broadly close commercial aviation in a qualifying region (https://www.intellinews.com/iran-suspends-general-aviation-and-vfr-flights-in-new-airspace-directive-421997/).

Warnings, No-Fly-Zones, or other flight restrictions imposed by airlines or countries other than Iran will not be sufficient for a “Yes” resolution.

Airspace closures which occur solely due to weather conditions will not qualify.

The primary resolution sources for this market will be official information from Iranian aviation authorities and a consensus of credible reporting.

eventMetadata.context_description: Trader consensus on Polymarket assigns a 16% implied probability for Iran to fully close its airspace by May 8—defined as complete suspension of commercial flights affecting at least two major airports like Tehran or Mashhad—and 41% by May 31, reflecting caution amid a shaky ceasefire in the U.S.-Iran war that began February 28. Iran's airspace partially reopened April 21 after earlier closures, but yesterday's Iranian missile and drone attacks on UAE oil facilities prompted UAE partial airspace restrictions and flight diversions, heightening regional aviation risks without triggering Iran's full shutdown. U.S. officials like Hegseth affirm the ceasefire holds for now, while Tehran announced new Strait of Hormuz oversight, with potential naval clashes or escalation signals eyed ahead of May deadlines.

title: US x Iran permanent peace deal by...?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if Iran and the United states agree to a permanent peace deal by the specified date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”. 

A permanent peace deal refers to any agreement which explicitly indicates that military hostilities between the United States and Iran have ended or will permanently cease, or uses equivalent language clearly signaling a lasting end to military hostilities between the United States and Iran. Agreements that are explicitly temporary or which do not include a definitive agreement to end military hostilities between the US and Iran on a lasting basis (e.g. a temporary extension of the two-week ceasefire agreement announced on April 7, 2026), will not qualify.

A qualifying agreement will be considered to have been established if either of the following conditions are met:

- The United States and Iran each sign or formally adopt a written agreement (e.g. a treaty or multi-point agreement) which meets the above criteria.

- Both the governments of the United States and Iran provide clear public confirmation that a qualifying agreement has been definitively established. Negotiations, statements of progress, or other statements which do not constitute a definitive announcement that a qualifying agreement has been reached will not count.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from the governments of the United States and Iran; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

eventMetadata.context_description: A fragile ceasefire, agreed April 8 via Pakistani mediation following US and Israeli strikes on Iran, faces mounting tests from recent Strait of Hormuz incidents, including Iranian claims of firing on US vessels and Washington's launch of Project Freedom to escort ships on May 4. President Trump rejected Tehran's latest 14-point peace proposal on May 1 as unacceptable over nuclear enrichment, ballistic missiles, sanctions relief, and proxy support, though envoy Steve Witkoff reports resumed indirect talks with Iran reviewing a US counteroffer. Sticking points echo past JCPOA failures, tempering trader optimism for near-term deals amid escalation risks, while longer timelines reflect potential diplomatic breakthroughs before year-end. No direct negotiations are scheduled.

eventMetadata.context_description: Trader consensus on Polymarket prices Robert F. Kennedy Jr. as the narrow frontrunner for the Republican presidential nomination in 2028 at 49%, reflecting his sustained popularity as HHS Secretary driving the Make America Healthy Again agenda and crossover appeal from his 2024 Trump endorsement, despite repeated public denials of a bid. Vice President J.D. Vance trails closely at 39% buoyed by incumbency and strong polling leads like the April CPAC straw poll (53%) and Yale Youth Poll (43%), though recent GOP donor whispers question his electability amid failed Iran negotiations and fundraising pushes. Marco Rubio's 21% share has climbed on reports of donor preferences over Vance and hawkish foreign policy contrasts, keeping the post-Trump primary field fluid ahead of 2026 midterms.

title: Will the U.S. invade Iran before 2027?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the United States commences a military offensive intended to establish control over any portion of Iran by December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

For the purposes of this market, land de facto controlled by Iran or the United States as of November 4, 2025 12:00 PM ET, will be considered the sovereign territory of that country.

The resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible sources.

markets.question: Will the U.S. invade Iran before 2027?
markets.description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the United States commences a military offensive intended to establish control over any portion of Iran by December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

For the purposes of this market, land de facto controlled by Iran or the United States as of November 4, 2025 12:00 PM ET, will be considered the sovereign territory of that country.

eventMetadata.context_description: Amid a fragile three-week ceasefire holding since late April 2026, trader consensus on Polymarket reflects low odds of a U.S. ground invasion of Iran before 2027, driven by ongoing diplomatic efforts and public opposition to escalation. President Trump is reviewing Tehran's latest proposal to end hostilities and reopen the Strait of Hormuz, following U.S. rejection of a prior offer, while signaling a "possibility" of renewed airstrikes but no ground commitment. Polls show majority American resistance to troop deployments, and Pentagon plans for operations like seizing Kharg Island remain unexecuted amid billions spent on air campaigns. With negotiations prioritizing de-escalation over full-scale military intervention, traders price significant barriers to invasion despite persistent tensions.

title: Eurovision Winner 2026
description:
This market will resolve to the country whose candidate for Eurovision 2026 wins.

eventMetadata.context_description: WTI crude oil front-month futures traded around $102 per barrel on May 5, 2026, down over 5% from recent highs near $115, reflecting profit-taking after a sharp EIA-reported draw of 6.2 million barrels in stockpiles for the week ended April 24 that affirmed U.S. net exporter status amid robust exports. Steady U.S. rig counts at 408 signal sustained shale output near record highs, counterbalancing OPEC+ gradual production increases and easing Strait of Hormuz tensions, while softer global demand forecasts from Goldman Sachs and EIA—citing China stockpiling and economic headwinds—cap upside. Traders eye this week's EIA inventory release on May 7 and OPEC+ monitoring for supply signals, with Brent implied peaks projected at $115 in Q2 before easing.

title: Elon Musk # tweets May 1 - May 8, 2026?
description:
This market will resolve according to the number of times Elon Musk (@elonmusk), posts on X from May 1 12:00 PM ET to May 8, 2026 12:00 PM ET.

For the purposes of this market, only main feed posts, quote posts and reposts will count.

Replies will NOT count towards the total - however, replies on the main feed such as https://x.com/elonmusk/status/1786073478711353576 will be counted by the tracker.

Deleted posts will count as long as they remain available long enough to be captured by the tracker (~5 minutes).

Community reposts which are not counted by the tracker not count toward the total.

The resolution source for this market is the 'Post Counter' figure for posts found at https://xtracker.polymarket.com. Individual posts can be viewed by clicking "Export Data". If the tracker does not update correctly in accordance with the rules, X itself may be used as a secondary resolution source.

eventMetadata.context_description: Trader consensus on Polymarket closely splits between 160-179 tweets (36.5% implied probability) and 180-199 (27.5%), reflecting Elon's elevated early-May pace of over 25 posts per day through May 5—107 confirmed via X trackers—driven by xAI's Grok 4.3 API launch, Starlink's Singapore Airlines deal announcements, and commentary on cultural flashpoints like the Palisades fires. Post-OpenAI trial testimony, which briefly curbed activity to ~16 daily, his rebound has fueled this momentum, with 108 posts logged by May 5 evening (71% into the May 1 12PM ET to May 8 12PM ET window). Key swing factors include potential viral spikes from Tesla/SpaceX updates or political memes in the final days versus a typical weekend slowdown, underscoring the volatility of Musk's real-time social media dominance as a pop culture force.

title: LoL: Hanwha Life Esports vs DN SOOPers (BO3) - Esports World Cup Korea Qualifier Playoffs
description:
This market refers to the LoL Upper bracket quarterfinal 1 match between Hanwha Life Esports and DN SOOPers in the Esports World Cup Korea Qualifier Playoffs, initially scheduled for May 5 at 4:00AM ET.

This market will resolve to "Hanwha Life Esports" if Hanwha Life Esports win the match against DN SOOPers.

This market will resolve to "DN SOOPers" if DN SOOPers win the match against Hanwha Life Esports.

If the match is canceled (not played at all), ends in a tie, or is delayed beyond 7 days from the scheduled date without a winner determined, this market will resolve to 50-50. 

If the match begins but is not completed, and one team wins due to the opponent's forfeiture, disqualification, or walkover, this market will resolve to the team who wins. 

If the match ends in a forfeit, disqualification, or walkover (team withdraws before the start and the other wins automatically), this market will resolve to 50-50. 

The resolution source for this market will be official information from https://gol.gg/esports/home. However, if https://gol.gg/esports/home has not published final results within 2 hours after the event’s conclusion, a consensus of credible reporting may be used instead including video evidence.

In cases where a team’s listed name includes minor discrepancies from the resolution source, this market will resolve based on the underlying real-world match rather than exact name matching. Recognizable abbreviations, alternate or erroneous spellings, sponsor tags, affiliate or academy designations, regional identifiers, and minor formatting differences will be treated as referring to the same team, provided the intended team can be clearly and uniquely identified within the relevant competition. If a listed team name has no reasonable connection to any participating team, or if it matches or could reasonably refer to another team in the same competition such that the intended team cannot be unambiguously determined, this market will resolve 50-50.

markets.question: Game 1: Any Player Quadra Kill?
markets.description:
This market is about whether any player achieves a Quadra Kill during Game 1. In League of Legends, a Quadra Kill occurs when a single player kills 4 enemy champions in rapid succession.

This market will resolve to "Yes" if any player on either team achieves a Quadra Kill during Game 1. This market will resolve to "No" if no player achieves a Quadra Kill. A Penta Kill (5 kills in rapid succession) also counts as a Quadra Kill having occurred for the purposes of this market.

If the match is canceled (not played at all) or is delayed beyond 7 days from the scheduled date, this market will resolve to 50-50.

If Game 1 is never played due to forfeit, disqualification, or walkover, this market will resolve to 50-50.

If Game 1 is not played because the series result has already been determined (e.g., a team clinches the series before Game 1 is needed), this market will resolve to 50-50.

If Game 1 begins but is not completed and ends via surrender, this market will resolve based on whether a Quadra Kill occurred prior to stoppage. If no Quadra Kill occurred, this market will resolve to "No".

If Game 1 is remade, resolution will be based on the remade game only.

The resolution source for this market will be official information from https://gol.gg/esports/home. However, if https://gol.gg/esports/home has not published final results within 2 hours after the event's conclusion, a consensus of credible reporting may be used instead including video evidence.

title: Next French Presidential Election
description:
The next French presidential election is currently expected to be held around April 2027.  This market pertains to the outcome of the next French presidential election, regardless of whether it follows the scheduled end of the current term or is held earlier. 

The President of France is elected via a two-round system; a candidate must secure over 50% of the vote to win outright in the first round. If no candidate achieves this, the top two contenders advance to a runoff.

This market will resolve according to the candidate who wins this election.

This market includes any potential second round. If, for any reason, the results of the election are not known by December 31, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Other".

This market will resolve based on the result of the election as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve based solely on the official results as reported by the French Government, specifically the Ministry of the Interior (https://www.interieur.gouv.fr/).

The next French presidential election is currently expected to be held around April 2027.  This market pertains to the outcome of the next French presidential election, regardless of whether it follows the scheduled end of the current term or is held earlier. 

The President of France is elected via a two-round system; a candidate must secure over 50% of the vote to win outright in the first round. If no candidate achieves this, the top two contenders advance to a runoff.

This market will resolve according to the candidate who wins this election.

This market includes any potential second round. If, for any reason, the results of the election are not known by December 31, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Other".

This market will resolve based on the result of the election as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve based solely on the official results as reported by the French Government, specifically the Ministry of the Interior (https://www.interieur.gouv.fr/).

The next French presidential election is currently expected to be held around April 2027.  This market pertains to the outcome of the next French presidential election, regardless of whether it follows the scheduled end of the current term or is held earlier. 

The President of France is elected via a two-round system; a candidate must secure over 50% of the vote to win outright in the first round. If no candidate achieves this, the top two contenders advance to a runoff.

This market will resolve according to the candidate who wins this election.

This market includes any potential second round. If, for any reason, the results of the election are not known by December 31, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Other".

This market will resolve based on the result of the election as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve based solely on the official results as reported by the French Government, specifically the Ministry of the Interior (https://www.interieur.gouv.fr/).

eventMetadata.context_description: Jordan Bardella's trader consensus lead at 23.5% reflects his consistent first-round polling dominance around 35% in late April Harris Interactive data, bolstered by National Rally momentum despite municipal election setbacks in March where the party failed to capture major cities. Édouard Philippe trails closely at 20.5% after strong reelection as Le Havre mayor and favorable runoff polls, such as Odoxa’s 52-48 edge over Bardella, positioning him as the center-right anti-RN bulwark amid Marine Le Pen’s ineligibility. Jean-Luc Mélenchon’s May 3 candidacy announcement consolidates some left support at 13%, but fragmentation across left and conservative fields—exemplified by Les Républicains nominating Bruno Retailleau—keeps the race tight one year from the April 2027 vote. Separation could arise from primary resolutions, senatorial elections in September, or economic shocks tipping anti-incumbent turnout.

title: Wild vs. Avalanche
description:
In the upcoming NHL game, scheduled for May 5 at 9:00PM ET:
If the Wild win, the market will resolve to "Wild".
If the Avalanche win, the market will resolve to "Avalanche".
If the game is postponed, this market will remain open until the game has been completed.
If the game is canceled entirely, with no make-up game, this market will resolve 50-50.
The result will be determined based on the final score including any overtime periods and shootouts. In the event of a shootout, one goal will be added to the winning team's score for the purpose of resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description: In the Western Conference second-round Stanley Cup Playoffs series, the Colorado Avalanche grabbed a 1-0 lead with a wild 9-6 Game 1 victory over the Minnesota Wild on May 3, fueled by Cale Makar's two third-period goals after an in-game injury scare and Nathan MacKinnon's three points amid 15 total goals from 14 scorers. Minnesota, missing shutdown center Joel Eriksson Ek and top-four defenseman Jonas Brodin for the first two games due to lower-body injuries, struggled defensively, prompting a goaltender switch to Filip Gustavsson for Game 2 after Jesper Wallstedt allowed nine goals. Colorado's Josh Manson remains out with an upper-body issue, but home-ice advantage at Ball Arena through Game 2 bolsters the top-seeded Avalanche (55-16-11 regular season), who boast superior firepower against a resilient third-seed Wild (46-24-12) in their fourth playoff clash.

title: Will __ ships transit the Strait of Hormuz on any day by end of April?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if IMF Portwatch publishes a daily number of transit calls (“Arrivals of Ships”) for the Strait of Hormuz equal to or above the listed value for any date between market creation and April 30, 2026. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

The number of daily transit calls/arrivals includes container, dry bulk, roll-on/roll-off, general cargo, and tanker ships. Ships not reported by IMF Portwatch will not be considered.

This market will resolve as soon as IMF Portwatch publishes a daily number of transit calls equal to or above the specified level, or once data has been published for the final date in the specified period and no such value has been published. If no data has been published for the final date of the specified period within 14 calendar days (ET) after the end of that period, this market will resolve based on data published up to that point.

Revisions to previously published data points, made within this market’s timeframe, will be considered. However, they will not disqualify a previously published data point from qualifying. Revisions to previously published data points after data is published for April 30, 2026, however, will not be considered.

The resolution source for this market will be IMF Portwatch, specifically the transit calls data published for the Strait of Hormuz at https://portwatch.imf.org/pages/cb5856222a5b4105adc6ee7e880a1730, both in the chart and through downloadable files.

series.title: __ ships transit the Strait of Hormuz on any day

eventMetadata.context_description: Trader consensus on Polymarket prices near-certainty against 40 or more ships transiting the Strait of Hormuz on any day through April 30, 2026, with Yes shares for the 40+ outcome trading at just 2% implied probability, reflecting IMF Portwatch data showing daily arrivals capped below 30 amid the ongoing 2026 Strait crisis. Iran's blockade since late February slashed volumes from pre-conflict averages of 130 vessels per day to 5-24, enforced via northern corridor controls and a 15-vessel daily limit, while U.S. countermeasures targeted Iran-linked shipping. This chokepoint disruption—handling 21% of global seaborne oil trade—has embedded a $10-15 per barrel risk premium into Brent crude, now above $110. Resolution awaits final IMF clarification on disputed April 27 data; U.S. "Project Freedom" escorts paused May 5 amid Pakistan-mediated ceasefire talks.

title: Presidential Election Winner 2028
description:
The 2028 US Presidential Election is scheduled to take place on November 7, 2028.

This market will resolve to the person who wins the 2028 US Presidential Election. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No.”

The resolution source for this market is the Associated Press, Fox News, and NBC. This market will resolve once all three sources call the race for the same candidate. If all three sources haven’t called the race for the same candidate by the inauguration date (January 20, 2029) this market will resolve based on who is inaugurated.

The 2028 US Presidential Election is scheduled to take place on November 7, 2028.

This market will resolve to the person who wins the 2028 US Presidential Election.

The resolution source for this market is the Associated Press, Fox News, and NBC. This market will resolve once all three sources call the race for the same candidate. If all three sources haven’t called the race for the same candidate by the inauguration date (January 20, 2029) this market will resolve based on who is inaugurated.

eventMetadata.context_description: Vice President JD Vance's Iowa debut this week, campaigning for Rep. Zach Nunn amid 2026 midterm battles, has cemented trader consensus on his 20.2% implied probability as the Republican heir apparent under President Trump, leveraging incumbency advantages and early caucus groundwork. California Gov. Gavin Newsom holds 17.1% as Democrats' leading post-2024 contender, while Sen. Marco Rubio's 10.8% reflects gains from his Secretary of State role during Iran tensions. The tight contest stems from the fluid pre-primary landscape, wide field, and uncertain paths to nomination; 2026 midterms, Trump's endorsements, polling shifts in swing states, economic trends, or scandals could widen gaps ahead of 2028 primaries.

title: Strait of Hormuz traffic returns to normal by May 15?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if IMF Portwatch publishes a 7-day moving average of transit calls (“Arrivals of Ships”) for the Strait of Hormuz equal to or above 60 for any date between market creation and May 15, 2026. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

Daily transit calls include container, dry bulk, roll-on/roll-off, general cargo, and tanker ships. Ships not reported by IMF Portwatch will not be considered.

This market will resolve as soon as IMF Portwatch publishes a 7-day moving average of transit calls equal to or above the specified level, or once data has been published for the final date in the specified period and no such value has been published. If no data has been published for the final date of the specified period within 14 calendar days (ET) after the end of that period, this market will resolve based on data published up to that point.

Revisions to previously published data points made within this market’s timeframe will be considered. However, they will not disqualify a previously published data point from qualifying. Revisions to previously published data points after data is published for May 31, 2026, however, will not be considered.

The resolution source for this market will be IMF Portwatch, specifically the transit calls data published for the Strait of Hormuz at https://portwatch.imf.org/pages/cb5856222a5b4105adc6ee7e880a1730, both in the chart and through downloadable files.

eventMetadata.context_description: Trader consensus prices "No" at 96.5% for Strait of Hormuz traffic returning to normal by May 15, driven by the ongoing US-Iran standoff that has slashed commercial transits to near zero—down over 95% from pre-crisis levels of 125-140 vessels daily. Recent escalation, including Iran's missile and drone strikes on military and commercial targets on May 4 and mutual blockades asserted by both sides as of May 5, has frozen shipping despite US initiatives to protect passage. No de-escalation signals have emerged since the February 28 crisis onset, with navigation data confirming restrictions to Iran-linked or pre-approved vessels only. A surprise ceasefire enforcement or bilateral negotiations could alter odds, but historical deadlock patterns suggest low likelihood before the deadline.

title: UEFA Champions League Winner
description: This is a polymarket to predict which club will win the 2025–26 UEFA Champions League (soccer).

markets.question: Will Real Madrid win the 2025–26 Champions League?
markets.description:
This is a polymarket on whether the listed team will win the 2025–26 UEFA Champions League.

This market will resolve to "Yes" if the listed team is officially crowned the winner of the 2025–26 UEFA Champions League. Otherwise, it will resolve to "No".

If at any point it becomes impossible for the listed team to win the tournament (e.g. they are mathematically eliminated), the market will resolve to "No".

If the 2025–26 UEFA Champions League is canceled or not completed by October 1, 2026, this market will resolve to "Other".

The primary resolution source will be official information from UEFA Champions League (https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/). A consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

eventMetadata.context_description: Arsenal leads trader consensus at 41.5% implied probability to win the UEFA Champions League after advancing to the final with aggregate victory over Atlético Madrid—1-1 first-leg draw away followed by home second-leg win at the Emirates on May 5—bolstered by robust knockout form including quarterfinal triumph over Sporting CP. Bayern Munich (31.5%) enters today's second leg at Allianz Arena with home advantage against PSG (28.5%), trailing 4-5 on aggregate from last week's nine-goal semi-final epic that exposed defensive frailties on both sides. Markets price a tight final matchup, factoring historical European pedigree, recent momentum, and potential for high-scoring chaos in the decider on May 30 at Puskás Aréna.

title: F1 Drivers' Champion
description:
This market will resolve according to the listed driver that finishes 1st in the driver standings for the 2026 F1 season.

This market will resolve as soon as the official results of the final scheduled race of the 2026 F1 season are known.

If multiple drivers tie for first place in the drivers standings, this market will resolve according to the tiebreak procedure used by F1 to determine the 2026 F1 Drivers’ champion.

If at any point it becomes impossible for a listed driver to win the 2026 F1 Drivers Championship based on the rules of F1 (e.g., they are mathematically eliminated from contention), the corresponding market will resolve to “No”.

If the F1 season is permanently canceled or has not been completed by February 28, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to “Other”.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from Formula 1.

title: Trump announces US blockade of Hormuz lifted by...?
description:
On April 12, 2026, President Donald Trump announced that the United States will blockade the Strait of Hormuz. You can read more about that here: https://www.nbcnews.com/world/iran/live-blog/live-updates-us-iran-fail-reach-deal-peace-talks-day-negotiations-rcna315918.

This market will resolve to "Yes" if President Trump, the US government, or the US military publicly and officially announces the end of the United States blockade of the Strait of Hormuz by the specified date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No."

Qualifying statements must clearly and explicitly indicate that the United States has lifted, ended, or will lift or end its blockade of the Strait of Hormuz on a specified date or use equivalently definitive language unambiguously signaling that such blockade has ceased or is set to cease on a specified date (e.g., statements unambiguously indicating that US naval activity in the relevant area has ceased will qualify). 

Statements that merely describe actions inconsistent with the blockade (e.g., "Iran resumed shipping through the Strait of Hormuz") without explicitly indicating the blockade as lifted will not alone suffice.

Informal announcements, statements from unnamed sources, or leaks do not qualify.

Written public statements from Donald Trump (e.g., posts from his personal Truth Social account) will qualify. Videos posted on his social media accounts will also qualify for a "Yes" resolution.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official statements from the US government and/or its official representatives; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

Note: this market will resolve solely based on whether a qualifying announcement is made within the specified timeframe. Whether the blockade is effectively enforced or whether maritime traffic resumes absent a qualifying announcement will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: President Trump announced on May 5 that the U.S. will pause Project Freedom—the naval operation to escort commercial ships through the Strait of Hormuz—for a short period to finalize a potential comprehensive agreement with Iran, while emphasizing the blockade of Iranian ports and ships remains fully in effect. This follows the blockade's imposition in mid-April after U.S.-Iran nuclear and regional talks collapsed, amid U.S. military actions destroying Iranian vessels and drones threatening strait traffic. The pause, requested by Pakistan and others, signals diplomatic progress that traders view as a precursor to lifting the blockade, though Tehran has not commented and escalation risks persist ahead of any deal signing or congressional briefings.

title: US x Iran diplomatic meeting by...?
description:

The resolution sources for this market will be official information from the governments of the United States and Iran, and a consensus of credible reporting.

eventMetadata.context_description: Amid a fragile ceasefire holding in the 2026 US-Iran conflict despite recent exchanges of fire in the Strait of Hormuz, trader sentiment hinges on stalled diplomatic efforts following mid-April's collapsed marathon talks in Islamabad, Pakistan—the first direct high-level meeting since 1979. Iran is reviewing a US response to its latest proposal conveyed via Pakistani intermediaries, with envoy Steve Witkoff noting active conversations, though President Trump dismissed it as likely unacceptable. Key sticking points include nuclear curbs, naval passage, and blockade enforcement, with no new in-person meeting scheduled. Upcoming catalysts could include proposal acceptance or escalation risks before potential June deadlines, underscoring uncertainty in bilateral negotiations.

PSG's 23.5% win probability reflects squad depth and rest advantage after Ligue 1 rotation, but defensive frailties exposed without Hakimi temper enthusiasm, leaving draw at 17.5% viable in a high-stakes knockout push.

eventMetadata.context_description: Xavier Becerra's surge in recent polls to 23-24% support, fueled by absorbing Eric Swalwell's voters after his mid-April withdrawal, has traders viewing him as the Democratic frontrunner in California's top-two primary on June 2, but billionaire Tom Steyer's $130 million self-funding and aggressive attack ads targeting Becerra's record as former attorney general keep the race neck-and-neck at near-even odds. The nonpartisan primary risks two Republicans—Steve Hilton or Chad Bianco—advancing if Democrats fragment further, though the state's deep-blue electorate favors a Democratic general election victory. A recent debate slightly boosted Steyer's momentum amid voter focus on affordability, homelessness, and crime, with consolidation endorsements or standout performances potentially creating separation before early voting ramps up.

title: Strait of Hormuz traffic returns to normal by end of May?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if IMF Portwatch publishes a 7-day moving average of transit calls (“Arrivals of Ships”) for the Strait of Hormuz equal to or above 60 for any date between market creation and May 31, 2026. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

Daily transit calls include container, dry bulk, roll-on/roll-off, general cargo, and tanker ships. Ships not reported by IMF Portwatch will not be considered.

This market will resolve as soon as IMF Portwatch publishes a 7-day moving average of transit calls equal to or above the specified level, or once data has been published for the final date in the specified period and no such value has been published. If no data has been published for the final date of the specified period within 14 calendar days (ET) after the end of that period, this market will resolve based on data published up to that point.

Revisions to previously published data points made within this market’s timeframe will be considered. However, they will not disqualify a previously published data point from qualifying. Revisions to previously published data points after data is published for May 31, 2026, however, will not be considered.

The resolution source for this market will be IMF Portwatch, specifically the transit calls data published for the Strait of Hormuz at https://portwatch.imf.org/pages/cb5856222a5b4105adc6ee7e880a1730, both in the chart and through downloadable files.

eventMetadata.context_description: Trader consensus prices "No" at 83.5% on Strait of Hormuz traffic returning to normal by May's end, reflecting a US-Iran military standoff that has slashed commercial transits to under 10% of prewar levels—typically 100+ vessels daily—since late February. Iran enforces strict navigation rules and restrictions, seizing ships and launching attacks, while US forces destroyed six Iranian boats on May 4 amid ongoing clashes. The Trump administration's "Project Freedom" escorts, begun May 3, enabled just six transits on day one, far below normal, as major carriers balk at risks without firm security pacts. Stalled diplomacy, stranded vessels exceeding 2,000, and soaring insurance premiums signal prolonged blockade effects despite prior ceasefire attempts.

eventMetadata.context_description: NVIDIA maintains a narrow market cap lead over Alphabet at approximately $4.8 trillion to $4.65 trillion, fueling trader consensus for a 52.6% implied probability of NVIDIA claiming the top spot by May's end amid intense AI-driven competition. Alphabet's recent Q1 earnings beat, with Google Cloud revenue surging 63% to $20 billion on robust artificial intelligence demand, sparked a 10% stock rally that erased over $400 billion in valuation gap within days, highlighting its diversified strengths in large language models like Gemini, search monetization, and cloud infrastructure. NVIDIA's edge stems from its GPU monopoly for AI training and inference, though custom chips like Alphabet's TPUs pose risks; upcoming May 20 earnings could solidify NVIDIA's position via data center growth updates.
